slides.heading: Repair Bst
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Binary Search Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Repair Bst, a hard binary search trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Exactly two nodes' values were swapped; swap them back in place.
Iterative in-order finds the two out-of-order nodes.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Exactly two nodes' values were swapped; swap them back in place. Iterative in-order finds the two out-of-order nodes.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: An in-order traversal of a BST is sorted; the two swapped nodes show up as order violations.
slides.narration: An in-order traversal of a BST is sorted; the two swapped nodes show up as order violations.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Copy in-order to array, sort, rewrite → O(n) space
In-order with prev pointer, catch the two violations → O(h) space
slides.narration: Dumping the in-order traversal into an array, sorting it and writing it back uses linear space. Tracking the previous node during an in-order walk spots the violations with only the stack.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. In-order traverse tracking the previous node
2. The first violation gives the first node
3. The last violation gives the second
slides.narration: Step by step. First, in-order traverse tracking the previous node. Second, the first violation gives the first node. Third, the last violation gives the second. Fourth, swap their values.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: A BST with two swapped values
slides.narration: Two values in this BST were swapped. We need to find and fix them.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: In-order should be sorted: drops at [12, 10] > [8, 7]
slides.narration: An in-order traversal of a BST is sorted. Here it drops: the first is the larger value before the first drop, 12, and the second is the smaller value after the last drop, 7.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Swap them back → valid BST
slides.narration: Swap those two values back and the in-order traversal is sorted again.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We do an iterative in-order traversal. When prev is greater than cur, the first time we record prev as first, and every time we record cur as second. Finally we swap their values.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: First = prev at first drop, second = cur at last drop
slides.narration: If the swapped nodes are adjacent in order, there's only one drop; the rule still works.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Mention Morris traversal for O(1) space
slides.narration: Mention Morris traversal for constant space.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: An in-order traversal of a BST is sorted; the two swapped nodes show up as order violations.
slides.narration: To recap Repair Bst: An in-order traversal of a BST is sorted; the two swapped nodes show up as order violations. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
